title: F1 in Brazil: You’ve got to keep your tires alive
gist: Recap of the Brazilian Grand Prix, where Lando Norris won from pole in mixed wet and dry conditions as tire management decided the race, Verstappen finished second after starting 21st, and Mercedes clinched the Constructors' title despite errors. The article is sports coverage with little investment relevance.

insights.claim: Tire operating-window management decided the Brazilian Grand Prix: Mercedes struggled to generate tire temperatures, and Hamilton's charge faded as his intermediate tires wore out.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Low investment relevance; illustrates performance sensitivity to tire strategy.

insights.claim: Lando Norris won from pole after Kimi Antonelli, the new champion, spun twice from the lead, with well-timed pit stops putting Norris on the right tires.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin

insights.claim: Max Verstappen started 21st and finished second, 14 seconds behind Norris, with his slower rear-tire warm-up probably aiding tire longevity.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin

insights.claim: Mercedes sealed the Constructors' Championship in Brazil despite fourth and fifth place finishes.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin

insights.claim: A defending F1 champion is not guaranteed a competitive car: McLaren did not start this year positioned to win races and its car remains tricky to drive even after several upgrades.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Illustrates regulation-cycle swings in team competitiveness.

insights.claim: Even with the championship settled, the Brazilian race was among the year's most entertaining, which the author uses to counter the idea that 'dead rubber' races lose viewers.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Minor media-engagement observation about sports formats.
insights.quote: The people in charge hate this

insights.claim: Hamilton's Brazil start was his 400th F1 race, and he has won more than a quarter of them.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
